pairs.old: More than 25% in the 90+ bucket signals a systemic problem.
pairs.new: A 90+ bucket well above the common ~15% target signals a systemic problem.
pairs.claim: fallback: more than 25% in 90+ signals a systemic problem
pairs.src: No source for a "25% in 90+" benchmark; the lesson body uses the common ~15% rule of thumb (internal contradiction). Medicare Claims Processing Manual ch.1 sec. 80.2: clean claims paid within 30 days of receipt — contradicts "most payers have not yet adjudicated" before 60 days

pairs.old: Industry benchmark is less than 25% of AR in the 90+ day bucket. A 35% concentration
pairs.new: Common industry targets keep 90+ AR to roughly 15% or less. A 35% concentration
pairs.claim: quiz explanation: industry benchmark less than 25% in 90+

pairs.old: Active follow-up before 60 days typically yields few results as most payers have not yet adjudicated the claim.
pairs.new: Medicare must pay clean claims within 30 days of receipt, so a claim still unpaid at 31–60 days warrants a status check, and one still unresolved past 60 days needs active follow-up.
